title: Level 2 order-book collector launched (data runway)
detail: Coinbase Advanced Trade WebSocket level2 channel (public, no auth) now feeds a 24/7 collector (src/data/l2_collector.py, systemd service tam-l2-collector, Restart=always + enabled). It maintains the full BTC-USD book (~14k bid / ~24k ask levels) and stores ONLY per-minute aggregates in data/l2_book.db (l2_minutes): mid, spread_bps, microprice deviation, order-book imbalance at +-0.1/0.5/1/2% depth bands, depth within 1%, top-of-book quantities, level counts, and true live coverage seconds per minute. Hourly rollups (l2_hours via src/data/l2_features.py) are causal by construction (hour H uses only minutes inside H) and carry a usable flag (minutes_present >= 50 AND mean coverage >= 55s); dead minutes are written with NULL features and true coverage, never faked. First genuinely new information source in the program -- everything previously graded recycled OHLCV (funding/OI, the only other exogenous family, failed at 1h). Verified at launch: 9 new hand-computed tests pass (15/15 with the cache smoke suite), live rows sane vs Coinbase spot, and a systemctl restart test reconnected, re-snapshotted and resumed with the interrupted minute honestly at 27.6s coverage. No trading/model/dashboard changes. Forward plan: collect ~6-8 weeks until 1,000+ usable hourly rows exist, then pre-register a Muse Pick on the L2 features (leading shape: a run-82-style entry gate). Design doc: refs/level2-collector-2026-11-18.md.

title: Trades tape (Time & Sales) added to the Level 2 collector
detail: Kass approved adding Coinbase's market_trades channel to the L2 collector on 2026-11-18; it rides the same websocket as a third subscription (level2 + heartbeats + market_trades, one connection, no auth). SIDE CONVENTION (verified against Coinbase's Advanced Trade docs): the trade `side` field is the MAKER (resting) order's side, so all accounting inverts it -- a print of side=BUY is SELL-initiated volume, side=SELL is BUY-initiated; pinned by tests (tests/test_l2_tape.py, 14 tests, watched failing first; 29/29 with the L2 + market-cache suites). Per-minute aggregates land in l2_trades_minutes (taker buy/sell/total BTC volume, trade counts, vwap, max print, large volume from prints >= 0.5 BTC, own coverage seconds) and roll up hourly into l2_trades_hours with signed_imbalance computed FROM THE SUMMED VOLUMES (never the mean of minute imbalances) and the same usable rule as the book side (minutes_present >= 50 AND coverage_mean >= 55). Prints are bucketed by trade time and deduped by trade_id; tape minutes finalize one minute behind book minutes to absorb Coinbase's ~250ms batching (cost: a restart loses the in-flight tape minute, written NULL/coverage 0, never reconstructed). The channel has no snapshot: outage trades are lost and coverage says so. Live verification: subscriptions confirmed; ~200-2,500 prints/min; over the full-coverage minutes 20:29-20:30 UTC the summed tape volume matched Coinbase's own 1-minute candle volume EXACTLY (19.2851 and 21.8869 BTC, +0.000%); a systemctl restart resumed both sides with honest partial coverage (book 34.5s / tape 34.4s). ENVIRONMENT: the VM was replaced at 20:08 UTC and the systemd unit did not survive the old instance's /etc -- the collector had been down since ~06:46 UTC (launch data 06:27-06:45 UTC intact); the unit is recreated from the copy now kept in-project at system/tam-l2-collector.service, service active + enabled. Full design + verification: refs/level2-collector-2026-11-18.md (Trades tape section). Data runway only -- no model until the pre-registered Pick is designed on ~1,000+ usable hours.
